narrative:
The model determined that you have a 58% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the property you own, and your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income. Your checking account status of less than 0 DM was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while 59% have no checking account at all. This negative status pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

Your lack of any registered property also worked against you. Most approved borrowers have either a car, real estate, or life insurance as assets; having nothing identifiable in this area further increased the perceived risk.

On a more positive note, your installment rate of 2% of disposable income was lower than the average of roughly 3% seen in approved loans. This lower rate helped push the prediction slightly toward approval, but it was not enough to overcome the negative effects of your account status and missing property.

To improve your chances next time, focus on clearing your checking account overdraft, building up verifiable assets, and maintaining steady employment. Once these areas look stronger, reapply or explore smaller loan amounts that better match your current financial profile.
